planets.name: HAT-P-7 b
planets.description: Transiting planet of HAT-P-7 with a 2.2-day year, found in 2008.

text.card: HAT-P-7 b was found in 2008 by HATNet as it crossed its star.
text.introduction: It is the only planet known around HAT-P-7. Its orbit and size follow Stassun et al. 2017's fit, the archive's default.
text.locator: NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table, default parameter set (pl_refname STASSUN_ET_AL__2017): disc_year 2008, disc_facility HATNet, sy_pnum 1; pl_orbper 2.2047354, pl_radj 1.51, pl_bmassj 1.84

quotes.title: HAT-P-7b
quotes.card: HAT-P-7b is an extrasolar planet discovered in 2008.
quotes.introduction: It orbits very close to its host star and is larger than Jupiter.

phaseCurves.label: Spitzer
phaseCurves.observed: a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 60021, first published by Wong et al. (2016))

record.source: Bell et al. (2021), MNRAS 504, 3316, 'A comprehensive reanalysis of Spitzer's 4.5 um phase curves, and the phase variations of the ultra-hot Jupiters MASCARA-1b and KELT-16b' (doi:10.1093/mnras/stab1027; arXiv:2010.00687). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of HAT-P-7b, program 60021, first published by Wong et al. (2016) and reanalysed here. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of preferred SPCA model parameters (tab:preferred), row HAT-P-7b, detector model BLISS. The preferred fit is first order (the caption of its figure names the mode BLISS_v1), so the printed semi-amplitude and offset are the whole phase variation (section 4.1: semi-amplitude sqrt(C1^2 + D1^2), offset east -arctan2(D1, C1)). The paper notes that its models prefer an unusually flat phase curve for HAT-P-7b compared with Wong et al. (2016), that the offset becomes poorly defined as the amplitude approaches zero, and that the offset scatters between its detector models by more than the fitted uncertainty.

model.equation: F_p = F_day [1 + C1 (cos psi - 1) + D1 sin psi], psi counted from mid-eclipse (section 4.1), printed as its semi-amplitude and the offset east of its maximum.
